keypoints.name: Wake Word Detection with TensorFlow Lite
keypoints.description: Using TensorFlow Lite on an ESP32 to create a system that continuously listens for a specific trigger word ("Marvin" in this case) to activate the system.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: The video dedicates a significant portion to explaining the process, from data acquisition to model training and conversion for the ESP32. It revisits the topic when discussing the ESP32 code.
representative_quotes: We're going to be using TensorFlow Lite for our wake word detection.
We have a very lightweight wake word detection system.

keypoints.name: Intent Recognition with Wit.ai
keypoints.description: Leveraging Facebook's Wit.ai service to analyze recorded speech after the wake word detection and determine the user's intended action.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: The video provides a demonstration of using Wit.ai, including training the application with sample phrases and testing it with recorded audio. It's also included in the final recap.
representative_quotes: So to do the heavy lifting of actually recognising the text we're going to be using a service from Facebook called Wit AI.
The witai system works very well and you can easily add your own intents and traits and build a very powerful system.

keypoints.name: ESP32 Code Integration
keypoints.description: Integrating the trained TensorFlow Lite model and Wit.ai service into the ESP32 microcontroller for a fully functional system.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: The video covers the ESP32 code structure, including libraries for TensorFlow Lite, audio input/output, and Wit.ai communication. The explanation comes late in the video.
representative_quotes: Let's have a look at how this is all wired up on the ESP32 side of things.
In our setup function we do all the normal work of setting up the serial port, connecting to WiFi and starting up SPFs.

keypoints.name: Spectrogram Feature Extraction
keypoints.description: Converting audio samples into spectrograms to turn the audio into something that looks like an image, which is a common step in approaching audio processing as an image recognition problem.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: This keypoint is given a dedicated explanation with code examples. The speaker also returns to it later when integrating it into the code running on the ESP32.
representative_quotes: To do this we can take a spectrogram of the audio sample.
We then generate the spectrogram. This spectrogram is fed directly into the neural network's input buffer so we can run the prediction.
